question: Should ClawHub/OpenClaw still support the legacy `curl -fsSL https://molt.bot/install.sh | zsh` install path, or should it be treated as retired in favor of the current `openclaw.ai` bash installer and documented ClawHub/OpenClaw commands?
rationale: The failing helper is absent from current ClawHub source while the live hosted URL redirects to an external OpenClaw installer, so automation cannot choose the support boundary or ownership model safely.

options.title: Retire or redirect legacy zsh usage
options.body: Point users to the current `openclaw.ai` bash installer and maintained ClawHub/OpenClaw install docs, then treat legacy zsh-piped failures as unsupported.

options.title: Own and harden the hosted installer
options.body: Track the installer source, reproduce the Homebrew/zsh cleanup failure, and add smoke proof or regression coverage for unmatched npm cleanup globs.

options.title: Wait for fresh reporter proof
options.body: Keep the issue waiting on author until there is current evidence that a supported installer path still fails.

recommendation.title: Retire or redirect legacy zsh usage
recommendation.body: Point users to the current `openclaw.ai` bash installer and maintained ClawHub/OpenClaw install docs, then treat legacy zsh-piped failures as unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen has the strongest current-history connection to the maintained ClawHub CLI/package install surface and already appears in the issue triage timeline.
